_metadata.purpose: x07: a bounded batch of owner suggestions (2026-10-19), processed locally with deterministic checks and a main-session critique; no model or review calls
_metadata.provenance: owner Deb West's suggestions and the parent's decisions, relayed by the coordinator (parent)
_metadata.workflow: owner suggestions are candidates, not approvals. One that passes the checks is added with catalogue add --by owner (source: owner suggestion), then accepted by the coordinator through an overrides.json coordinator_accept (not an owner decision). Holds and non-acceptances are recorded with their reasons so they are not proposed again by accident.
_metadata.checks: bank membership (catalogue show), existing hints and preferences for the pair, rejections.json, the catalogue hint rule (hintProblem), served uses of the same hint (random-library.json), facts in the explanation

items.outcome: held: hint syntax conflict, not added
items.detail: The catalogue's rule allows letters only, so K9 is refused. Older reviewed batches already hold K9 (DOG + ROBOT, unserved), and C3PO and R2D2 are served, so the rule and the library disagree. Not renamed (no CANINE or KNINE substitution). Needs a parent decision on allowing digits in well-known names; if allowed, K9 is a strong hint here: police dog units are called K-9 units.

items.why: Volcanoes erupt, and a room can erupt in laughter.
items.critique: Strong and natural: 'erupt in laughter' is an everyday phrase. VOLCANO already serves ERUPT once (SODA + VOLCANO), a small variety cost.

items.why: A harmonica is a musical instrument small enough to carry in your pocket.
items.critique: Fair and concrete. Another small instrument (KAZOO) would also fit, but HARMONICA is the classic pocket instrument.

items.why: Apple pie and pumpkin pie are two classic pies.
items.critique: Immediate on both sides. PIE was rejected for many other APPLE pairs where the second word has no pie; here both words are classic pies.

items.why: A calculator has a pi (π) button, and pi sounds like pie, as in pumpkin pie.
items.critique: A sound-alike pun on the PUMPKIN side, said plainly in the explanation. A harder but explainable stretch; the calculator side is direct.

items.outcome: not accepted (parent decision); recorded in rejections.json for this hint only
items.detail: The crossroads legend is about a deal with the devil, not purgatory. CROSSROADS is not in the word bank, so the pair cannot be stored in the library yet; it stays open.

items.outcome: candidate only (unselected); not stored, because CROSSROADS is not in the word bank
items.why: In the old legend, you make a deal with the devil at the crossroads.
items.detail: Stronger than PURGATORY, but not owner-selected. It can be added as a candidate only if CROSSROADS joins the bank (a separate decision).

items.outcome: owner-selected: stored and served (supersedes candidate-only status)
items.why: A rooster is a bird; penguins are the birds strongly associated with Antarctica.
items.detail: Deb West chose PENGUIN (2026-10-19): "Antarctica + type of bird = Penguin", a location-plus-category analogy. WADDLE (rooster wattle / penguin waddle) was a parent brainstorm only, not selected, not recorded as a hint.

items.why: A rooster is a bird; penguins are the birds most commonly associated with ice.
items.detail: Same analogy; says commonly associated with ice, not that all penguins live on ice.

items.outcome: blocked: FROZEN is not in the word bank (it is used only as a hint); not added, bank unchanged
items.detail: Can be added if FROZEN joins the bank (a separate decision).
